The three-node ring is the smallest nontrivial periodic network, and the three-loop nilpotent separatrix makes its critical slowing polynomial rather than the usual hyperbolic logarithmic delay. The exact beta coefficient measures an original-time physical observable, with a complete two-annulus classification to locate the orbits. This is a motivated structural finite-dimensional result, not arbitrary parameter tabulation.
